summary: The checked-out ASGI metrics app aggregated Prometheus multiprocess files synchronously on the server event loop. A deterministic 350 ms collector stall produced 331 ms of event-loop lag. Metrics generation now runs in a bounded child process, permits one active collection, and immediately returns 503 to concurrent scrapes. The same fixture produced 0 ms measured event-loop lag after the change.

tests.what_was_measured: Four focused cases covering slow isolated collection and singleflight rejection, timeout child cleanup, failed-child response behavior, and cancelled-request child cleanup; 4 passed.
A 350 ms metrics child delay left the ASGI event loop responsive (0.000 s measured lag), the active scrape returned 200, and a concurrent scrape returned 503.
The real subprocess collector read a multiprocess counter from disk and returned sglang_isolation_test_total 7.0 with status 200.
Changed Python files compiled and the patch had no whitespace errors. Ruff and Black were unavailable in the prepared interpreter.

remaining_limitations: No GPU was used because the corrected failure mechanism is confined to CPU-side ASGI scheduling and Prometheus multiprocess-file aggregation; GPU execution would not exercise it.
The original multi-node, single-tokenizer PD deployment on NVIDIA H100 hardware and its decode-side connection-loss logs were not reproduced in this single-gfx950 environment.
The deterministic regression validates the reported shared-event-loop starvation mechanism and HTTP overload behavior, not full-model semantics or a distributed workload.
The removed prototype commit was unavailable by its pinned hash; a surviving prototype branch was inspected and had a broader cached-snapshot design, which was not copied.
